::: {.callout-warning}
This is a formulation and sensitivity study around a fixed exploratory bundle.
It does not authorize a new parameter adoption or establish a universal
permittivity model.
:::

# Question

Which dielectric treatment is consistent with the retained ePC-SAFT
formulation, and can bounded changes to Born diameters, solvent mixing or
reaction temperature dependence resolve the pressure/speciation mismatch?

# Starting point and strategy

The study kept the molecular parameter packet, state packet and Engine identity
fixed while comparing the retained ion-specific formulation with derived
temperature/component mixing and the Uyan solvent-only mixing transferred from
MDEA to MEA. The later superseding study also screened original Born against
SSM+DS activation, Figiel and Zuber analog/fallback-ion choices, CO₂ pool
inclusion, and bounded joint sensitivity directions.

The active mapping is automatic: positive unique ion Born diameters with a
non-unit neutral solvation factor activate corrected SSM+DS; a zero Born
diameter inherits the Debye–Hückel diameter and recovers original Born. CO₂
remains an EOS component even when excluded from the salt-free neutral
permittivity pool.

# Numerical result

The earlier three-formulation comparison evaluated 120/123 total states. On
the common comparison, Uyan solvent-only mixing was closer on 53 pressure
targets and 77 speciation targets; Schick temperature mixing was closer on 12
pressure and 54 speciation targets. The comparison used a different parameter
and Engine identity from the current selected record, so those counts are
formulation evidence rather than current bundle scores.

The superseding fixed-bundle study retains the complete pressure/speciation
comparison, failure characterization, paired common-row statistics, parity
checks, density-anchor timing and bounded Born/solvation-factor sensitivity.
Its selected live mapping remains the switch-free selected JSON. The retained
joint direction improved selected rows only within the tested bounded screen;
it did not demonstrate separate ionic parameter identification.

# Conclusion and limits

Solvent-only mass-fraction dielectric mixing remains the selected working
formulation because it was the retained comparison choice under its declared
guards. The evidence supports a formulation decision for this bundle, not a
claim that Born diameters or dielectric mixing are independently fitted from
MEA observations. The pressure/speciation trade-off and preserved failures
must remain visible in any later regression or process-model claim.
